title: At the pharmacy
sentences: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, I have a headache. Do you have anything for it?
Take one tablet every six hours with water.
Thank you. How much is it?
It is four dollars.

questions.prompt: What problem does the customer have?
questions.explain: The customer says "I have a headache".

questions.prompt: How often should the customer take a tablet?
How much does the medicine cost, in dollars? (a number word)

title: Changing a meeting
sentences: Hi Nadia, are you free on Tuesday afternoon?
I have a dentist appointment at three, but I am free at one.
One o'clock is too early for me because I have a class.
How about Wednesday morning instead?
Wednesday at ten works well. I will send the invitation.

questions.prompt: Why can Nadia not meet at three on Tuesday?
questions.explain: She has a dentist appointment at three.

questions.prompt: When do they agree to meet?
questions.explain: They agree on Wednesday at ten.

questions.prompt: Who will send the invitation? (a name)
questions.explain: The final speaker, Nadia, says she will send it.

title: A delayed flight
sentences: Attention, passengers on flight 218 to Nairobi.
Due to bad weather, your flight is delayed by two hours.
The new departure time is six forty-five in the evening.
Meal vouchers are available at the information desk.
We apologise for the inconvenience.

questions.prompt: Where can passengers get meal vouchers?
questions.explain: Vouchers are at the information desk.

title: Feedback on a project
sentences: Overall, the report is well structured and easy to follow.
However, the conclusion could be stronger, because it does not mention the budget.
I would also suggest adding a short summary at the beginning.
If you can revise it by Friday, we can present it on Monday.
That is a fair point. I will make those changes.

questions.prompt: What is the main weakness mentioned?
options: The conclusion does not mention the budget
questions.explain: The speaker says the conclusion does not mention the budget.

questions.prompt: When must the report be revised?
What should be added at the beginning? (one word)
questions.explain: A short summary at the beginning.

title: A radio interview about remote work
sentences: Remote work has undeniably changed how companies recruit.
On the one hand, firms can hire talent from anywhere in the world.
On the other hand, managers struggle to build a shared culture across time zones.
The evidence suggests that productivity rises, provided that expectations are clear.
Ultimately, the success of the model depends on trust rather than on surveillance.

questions.prompt: What benefit of remote work is mentioned for recruitment?
questions.explain: Firms can hire talent from anywhere.

questions.prompt: According to the speaker, productivity rises if...
The success of the model depends on trust, not on... (one word)
questions.explain: The last sentence contrasts trust with surveillance.

title: A lecture on language change
sentences: Languages are never static; they evolve in response to the communities that use them.
What purists decry as corruption is frequently the seed of tomorrow's standard usage.
Consider how the word "nice" has drifted from meaning foolish to meaning pleasant.
Such shifts are rarely deliberate, and they seldom follow any predictable course.
The linguist's task is therefore to describe change, not to legislate against it.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker describe what purists call corruption?
options: Often the beginning of future standard usage
questions.explain: It is "frequently the seed of tomorrow's standard usage".

questions.prompt: What did the word "nice" originally mean in the example?
questions.explain: It drifted from meaning foolish to pleasant.

questions.prompt: The linguist should describe change, not... against it. (one word)
questions.explain: The last sentence says "not to legislate against it".
